newsitem.title: SWEDEN: MoDo says Alizay has cost 2 bln Skr since '91.
newsitem.headline: MoDo says Alizay has cost 2 bln Skr since '91.

text.p: Swedish forestry group MoDo said on Tuesday its French pulp and fine paper plant Alizay has cost two billion crowns in losses since it acquired the unit in 1991 for 3.5 billion crowns.
"In hindsight, we can state that the timing was poor," Hans Pettersson, the head of MoDo unit MoDo Paper, told Reuters.
After the acquisition, Alizay was hit by surprise after surprise.
"First the devaluation of the crown took 30 percent off income and then there was large technical problems when Alizay was being started up," Pettersson said.

"At the same time came the fall of the Soviet Union, which caused Finnish fine paper producers to turn from the Soviet Union to the French and European markets. Finnish producers took 20 percent of the French market."
Pettersson stressed that Alizay was breaking even at the moment, helped by making cut size A4 fine paper, a more expensive product than regular fine paper.
"It makes some money on paper and a bit less on pulp," he said.
